source: Direct user approval in this task; Sanctuary deviations take precedence over reference behavior.
userReport: i haven't observed that, and i don't think we need to make that distinction. monster corpse -> edible
observedReferenceBehavior: No new executable observation was claimed. The older engine's search and consume predicates differ; its consume path requires the soft-monster flag.
approvedDeviation: Dire Wolves may eat otherwise usable monster corpses regardless of skeletal, fleshy or other monster type. Do not impose source soft/material, dead-collision or corpse-selectable type restrictions on edibility.
preservedSharedRules: Use actual monster corpses, retaining the existing shared ownership, access and loot-preservation rules.
Reserve and consume each corpse only once; consumed, shattered or otherwise unavailable bodies are not restored by this rule.
Keep corpse-search range, first-eligible ordering, AI priority and the rage effect separate from this type-independent edibility rule.

implementation.verification: Real skeletal and fleshy monster deaths; selectable=false and missing source/base/seed controls; existing corpse-skill selectable gate retained; ownership/shatter/reservation/harvest/map exclusions; consume before buff service; failed allocation still consumes; repeated consumers refused; loot and empty-corpse cleanup; two actual corpse/body reloads. See dire-wolf-body-native-evidence.json.
implementation.next: Connect the accepted Fenris policy to saved world motion, acquisition and NPC314 animation/release. Replace the explicit rage-allocation service with the real 500-frame/+100% stat consumer, then physical combat and learned casting.
